questions.explanation: The one that does not fold is 6 squares — row 1 has column 3; row 2 has columns 2-3; row 3 has columns 1-3: four of its squares meet in a 2-by-2 block, and a block like that can never wrap round a cube — two of those squares would fold onto the same face. Each of the other three folds into a complete cube with every face covered exactly once.

questions.explanation: The net that folds is 6 squares — row 1 has column 1; row 2 has columns 1-3; row 3 has column 2; row 4 has column 2: every one of its six squares lands on a different face of the cube, so nothing is left open and nothing overlaps. The other three cannot work — one has a 2-by-2 block — so a face is doubled and another is left open.
